quests.question: She bought a sandwich ____ a bottle of water for lunch.
quests.sentence: She bought a sandwich ____ a bottle of water for lunch.
quests.hint: Both items were purchased together as part of the same lunch.
quests.explanation: 'And' joins two items bought in the same transaction. A sandwich AND a bottle of water were both purchased - 'or' would mean she chose between them.

quests.question: He went to bed early ____ he had an important presentation the next morning.
quests.sentence: He went to bed early ____ he had an important presentation the next morning.
quests.hint: The early night had a clear reason: the important morning ahead.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the reason for a decision. An important presentation (reason) explains going to bed early (action). 'So' would need the clauses reversed: 'He had a presentation, so he went to bed early.'

quests.question: She listened to a podcast ____ she drove to work.
quests.sentence: She listened to a podcast ____ she drove to work.
quests.hint: Listening and driving happened at the same time.
quests.explanation: 'While' connects two simultaneous activities. She listened to a podcast during the same time she was driving. Both happened together during the commute.

quests.question: Turn off all the lights ____ you leave the house.
quests.sentence: Turn off all the lights ____ you leave the house.
quests.hint: The lights must be switched off before leaving, not after.
quests.explanation: 'Before' shows the required prior action. Turning off lights BEFORE leaving saves energy and is a security measure. Doing it after leaving would be impossible.

quests.question: The film had excellent reviews ____ I found it quite boring.
quests.sentence: The film had excellent reviews ____ I found it quite boring.
quests.hint: Good reviews and personal boredom are in direct contrast.
quests.explanation: 'But' highlights the contrast between external praise (excellent reviews) and personal experience (finding it boring). Personal opinion can differ from critical consensus.

quests.question: She felt deeply relieved ____ she submitted her university application.
quests.sentence: She felt deeply relieved ____ she submitted her university application.
quests.hint: Submission happened first; the relief came right after that moment.
quests.explanation: 'After' places the relief following the submission. Submitting the application (action) led to relief (emotional response). The relief came AFTER the stressful task was completed.

quests.question: It was getting cold outside ____ she put on a warm jumper.
quests.sentence: It was getting cold outside ____ she put on a warm jumper.
quests.hint: Getting cold was the reason she needed a jumper.
quests.explanation: 'So' shows the result. The cold outside (cause) led her to put on a jumper (result). 'And' would just list two facts without showing the causal link.

quests.question: I will go to the gym ____ I finish work before six o'clock.
quests.sentence: I will go to the gym ____ I finish work before six o'clock.
quests.hint: Finishing before six is the condition for going to the gym.
quests.explanation: 'If' introduces a condition. Going to the gym only happens IF work finishes before six. 'When' would assume this definitely happens - 'if' shows it's conditional.

quests.question: The restaurant had a long queue ____ the food was absolutely worth the wait.
quests.sentence: The restaurant had a long queue ____ the food was absolutely worth the wait.
quests.hint: A long queue would usually put people off - but the food made it worthwhile.
quests.explanation: 'Yet' contrasts a negative aspect (long queue) with a positive outcome (worth the wait). This shows a surprising or positive result despite an obstacle.

quests.question: He kept refreshing his inbox ____ the booking confirmation finally arrived.
quests.sentence: He kept refreshing his inbox ____ the booking confirmation finally arrived.
quests.hint: Refreshing continued right up to the moment the email arrived.
quests.explanation: 'Until' marks the endpoint of a repeated action. He kept refreshing UNTIL the email arrived (the stopping point). At that moment, the refreshing stopped because the goal was achieved.

quests.question: You can pay by card ____ use the automated self-service machine.
quests.sentence: You can pay by card ____ use the automated self-service machine.
quests.hint: Two payment methods are available - the customer can choose one.
quests.explanation: 'Or' offers a choice between two alternatives. Card payment OR self-service - the customer only needs to choose one method, not use both.

quests.question: She wore thick socks indoors ____ her feet were always cold.
quests.sentence: She wore thick socks indoors ____ her feet were always cold.
quests.hint: Cold feet are the direct reason she needed thick socks.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the personal reason for a habit. Cold feet (cause) explain wearing thick socks (habit). 'So' would need the clauses reversed: 'Her feet were always cold, so she wore thick socks.'

quests.question: He ordered a coffee ____ a large slice of carrot cake at the café.
quests.sentence: He ordered a coffee ____ a large slice of carrot cake at the café.
quests.hint: Both items were ordered together at the café.
quests.explanation: 'And' joins two items in the same order. He ordered coffee AND cake - both were part of the same café visit. 'Or' would mean he chose between them.

quests.question: She listened to an audiobook ____ she commuted on the train.
quests.sentence: She listened to an audiobook ____ she commuted on the train.
quests.hint: Listening and commuting happened at the same time.
quests.explanation: 'While' connects two simultaneous activities. She listened to the audiobook during the commute - both happened over the same period of time on the train.

quests.question: The sports centre is nearby ____ it is always extremely crowded.
quests.sentence: The sports centre is nearby ____ it is always extremely crowded.
quests.hint: Being nearby is convenient - but being crowded is a drawback.
quests.explanation: 'But' contrasts a positive attribute (nearby location) with a negative drawback (always crowded). The sentence acknowledges the good and bad aspects of the same place.

quests.question: She had a light snack ____ the dinner party was due to start.
quests.sentence: She had a light snack ____ the dinner party was due to start.
quests.hint: The snack was eaten before the dinner party, not after.
quests.explanation: 'Before' shows prior timing. She ate the snack BEFORE the dinner party - perhaps to avoid being too hungry or to tide herself over. Eating after would be the dinner itself.

quests.question: The printer ran out of ink ____ she had to rush to the shops.
quests.sentence: The printer ran out of ink ____ she had to rush to the shops.
quests.hint: Running out of ink caused the urgent trip to the shops.
quests.explanation: 'So' shows the consequence. Running out of ink (cause) made her rush to the shops (result). 'And' would just list two events without showing why one caused the other.

quests.question: He will join the cycling team ____ they can offer flexible training hours.
quests.sentence: He will join the cycling team ____ they can offer flexible training hours.
quests.hint: Flexible hours are his condition for joining.
quests.explanation: 'If' introduces the condition. He will only join IF they offer flexible hours. 'When' would assume flexibility is guaranteed - 'if' shows it must be confirmed first.

quests.question: The documentary was over three hours long ____ it felt far too short.
quests.sentence: The documentary was over three hours long ____ it felt far too short.
quests.hint: Feeling short after three hours is a very surprising contrast.
quests.explanation: 'Yet' expresses a surprising or paradoxical reaction. A three-hour documentary feeling too short is unexpected and almost contradictory - 'yet' captures that sense of pleasant surprise.

quests.question: She kept the radio on ____ she worked from home all day.
quests.sentence: She kept the radio on ____ she worked from home all day.
quests.hint: The radio played throughout the whole working day - both happened simultaneously.
quests.explanation: 'While' shows a state maintained during another ongoing activity. The radio was on throughout the entire time she was working from home.

quests.question: The shop was closed ____ it was a public holiday that day.
quests.sentence: The shop was closed ____ it was a public holiday that day.
quests.hint: A public holiday is the direct official reason for the shop being closed.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the clear, factual reason. The public holiday (cause) explains the closure (result). 'So' would need the clauses reversed.

quests.question: They went for a walk in the park ____ they had finished Sunday lunch.
quests.sentence: They went for a walk in the park ____ they had finished Sunday lunch.
quests.hint: Lunch was eaten first; the walk came after.
quests.explanation: 'After' shows chronological sequence. They had lunch (first activity), then went for a walk (second activity). This is the natural post-meal routine.

quests.question: You can see a GP at the surgery ____ go to the walk-in clinic instead.
quests.sentence: You can see a GP at the surgery ____ go to the walk-in clinic instead.
quests.hint: Two options for getting medical help - choose the more convenient one.
quests.explanation: 'Or' offers two alternative healthcare options. Patients can visit the GP OR go to the walk-in clinic - only one visit is needed.

quests.question: She sent the email ____ immediately called the client to follow up.
quests.sentence: She sent the email ____ immediately called the client to follow up.
quests.hint: Both communication actions were done in quick succession.
quests.explanation: 'And' joins two sequential actions done as part of the same communication effort. She sent the email and then called - both actions were done, one after the other.

quests.question: He waited patiently outside the theatre ____ the doors opened.
quests.sentence: He waited patiently outside the theatre ____ the doors opened.
quests.hint: Waiting continued right up to the moment the doors opened.
quests.explanation: 'Until' marks the endpoint. He waited UNTIL the doors opened (the stopping point). At that moment, the waiting ended and he could enter.

quests.question: The hotel looked stunning in the photos ____ it was a real disappointment in person.
quests.sentence: The hotel looked stunning in the photos ____ it was a real disappointment in person.
quests.hint: Photos and reality were very different - that contrast is the key.
quests.explanation: 'But' contrasts expectations (stunning photos) with reality (disappointment). This is a common experience when something looks better online than in real life.

quests.question: She missed the last bus ____ had to order a taxi home.
quests.sentence: She missed the last bus ____ had to order a taxi home.
quests.hint: Missing the bus caused the need for a taxi.
quests.explanation: 'So' shows the consequence. Missing the last bus (cause) meant having to order a taxi (result). 'And' would just list two things that happened without explaining why.

quests.question: He always checks the weather forecast ____ he plans a day trip.
quests.sentence: He always checks the weather forecast ____ he plans a day trip.
quests.hint: Checking the forecast happens first, before making trip plans.
quests.explanation: 'Before' shows prior action. Checking the forecast BEFORE planning ensures the trip goes ahead in good weather. Checking after planning would be too late to change the plan.

quests.question: She completed the crossword ____ then made herself a pot of tea.
quests.sentence: She completed the crossword ____ then made herself a pot of tea.
quests.hint: Both activities happened - first the crossword, then the tea.
quests.explanation: 'And' joins two sequential leisure activities. She finished the crossword first and then made tea - both things happened, one after the other.

quests.question: He always says thank you ____ someone holds a door open for him.
quests.sentence: He always says thank you ____ someone holds a door open for him.
quests.hint: Someone holding a door is the regular trigger for saying thank you.
quests.explanation: 'When' connects a recurring social trigger (someone holding a door) to a regular polite response (saying thank you). This happens consistently - 'if' would imply uncertainty about whether people hold doors.
